JPM.rationale: JPM presents a strong fundamental case: Q1-26 EPS of $5.94 grew +17.2% YoY on +10.0% revenue growth, with stable 31.5% net margin and ROE improving to 16.2% — the highest in the observed window. The franchise is best-in-class with ~20% core ROTCE, dominant deposit base, and genuine revenue diversification across NII and fee income (AWM AUM $4.48T, payments +9% YoY, trading +17%). Valuation has compressed to 14.5x P/E from a 17.5x peak despite improving fundamentals — the market is paying less for better earnings power. The SpaceX IPO mandate (2026-06-04) is a credible near-term fee catalyst reinforcing franchise dominance. Offsets include expense guidance creep to $106B, DOJ debanking subpoena (2026-06-11), yield-curve flattening (10Y-2Y narrowed from 55bp to 40bp), and a $13B G-SIB surcharge risk. The score sits between mildly and strongly attractive: fundamentals and trajectory are solid, valuation is cheap vs own history, and a dated catalyst exists, but regulatory/legal overhang and curve flattening temper conviction below +0.5.

AWM AUM $4.48T (+18%), $52B long-term net inflows; payments revenue +9% YoY; trading revenues +17% (equities +40%) — genuine revenue diversification

Expense guidance raised to ~$106B from $105B (2026-05-27); $10–20B acquisition war-chest signals investment priority over near-term margin expansion

Stock at $313.49, 7% below 52-week high of $337.25 despite fundamental improvement — price has not fully reflected earnings acceleration
